Ñanderu Mbaecuaá.note: As Tyvyry’s attributed father, he establishes the brothers’ differentiated paternity without a prominent direct encounter.

Ñanderu Mbaekuaa.note: Tyvýry belongs to the dual-paternity genealogy involving Ñanderu Mbaekuaa.

Ñanderu Mba’ekuaa.note: He fathers the astral brothers and, in some readings, the junior hero.

Ñanderuvuçú.note: Ñanderyke’y belongs to the Apapocúva dual-paternity genealogy involving the great creator.
Ñanderyke’y seeks or communicates with his creator-father and approaches his celestial sphere.
In the Apapokúva recension, Ñanderyke’y is Ñanderuvuçú’s elder son.

Ñanderuvuçú.myth: Ritual communication with the absent father
Ñanderuvuçú.note: Ñanderyke’y communicates with his departed father through shamanic song and dance, receiving power or direction.
Later scholarship compares or equates this Apapocúva creator with Ñamandu, without a narrative meeting.
His created world is destroyed; Yvy Marã Ey remains the sought refuge.

Ñanderýke’y.note: He removes the earth’s eastern support, causing the catastrophe escaped through Yvy Marã Ey.

Ñane Ramõi Jusu Papa.note: He is her father-in-law in the differentiated Paĩ divine genealogy.
Conflated accounts transfer the younger pair’s marital quarrel to the older pair.
